DM1 hackathon: which covariates matter and which method predicts best

Team 1 · Wenzhe Ma · simulated data · every method in the kickoff guide · results repeated over 20 different 1:3 train/test splits · detailed code-level report: summary_split1to3.html

Key findings
  1. Same drivers whatever the method. Mexiletine: Myotonia severity (20/20 methods, continuous outcome); Oligonucleotide: CTG repeat length (16/20 methods, continuous outcome); Tideglusib: Cognitive function (20/20 methods, continuous outcome). Other covariates are retained by far fewer methods.
  2. The best methods of both tracks are equivalent. Best single methods on average R²: Random forest (tuned) (0.41); best covariate model Smoothing spline (top-1) (0.40); best ML Random forest (tuned) (0.41). Averaged over all methods in a track, ML is lower; the 95% range over splits excludes zero in Mexiletine, Oligonucleotide (ML minus covariate R²: Mexi. -0.07, Olig. -0.18, Tide. -0.01) because MLP, KNN and SVM do poorly on ~120 patients; tree ensembles (forest, XGBoost) match the best covariate models in Mexiletine, fall behind them in Oligonucleotide, and beat them only in Tideglusib (mean R² ≈ 0.52 vs ≈ 0.43; non-linear muscle-strength effect).
  3. Predictability differs by arm: Mexiletine best mean test R² 0.66, Oligonucleotide best mean test R² 0.14, Tideglusib best mean test R² 0.53.
  4. Results are split-dependent: the SD across the 20 seeds (error bars) is often as large as the gaps between neighbouring methods, so only large, consistent differences should be quoted.

0. Design in one paragraph

Each arm is modelled separately. For each of 20 random seeds the patients were split 75/25 (outcome-quartile strata, then covariate re-randomisation; worst train-test covariate imbalance 0.23-0.26 SD on average vs 0.36 for plain random splits). All 30 methods were fitted on the training part only and scored on the test part (≈41-43 patients). Tables and bars below are mean ± SD over the 20 splits. A covariate is retained by a method when the method selects it (rule per method below) in ≥ 70% of the splits, which guards against chance picks from a single split.

1. What the variables mean

Variable name in data Plain name Meaning Domain
ctg_repeats (shown as log10) CTG repeat length CTG trinucleotide repeat length in DMPK; the classic genetic severity marker Genetic burden
somatic_mosaicism_index Somatic mosaicism Variability of repeat length across a patient's tissues (0-1) Genetic burden
age_at_onset Age at onset Age (years) when symptoms first appeared Disease stage
disease_duration Disease duration Years since symptom onset (age - age at onset) Disease stage
age Age (not modelled) Current age; omitted because it equals onset age + duration Disease stage
phenotype DM1 subtype juvenile / adult / late onset pattern Disease stage
myotonia_severity Myotonia severity Baseline delayed muscle relaxation, 0-10 (higher = worse) Muscle
muscle_strength Muscle strength Composite strength score, 20-100 (higher = stronger) Muscle
ck_level Creatine kinase Baseline CK (U/L), marker of muscle damage Muscle
pr_interval ECG PR interval Cardiac conduction time (ms) Cardiac
cognitive_function Cognitive function Standardised cognitive performance z-score vs population (higher = better) CNS
insulin_resistance Insulin resistance HOMA-IR index Metabolic
bmi BMI Body mass index (kg/m2) Systemic
albumin Serum albumin g/dL, nutritional/hepatic marker (constant in the Mexiletine arm, so dropped there) Systemic
smoking_status Smoking never / former / current Systemic
sex Sex male / female Demographic
family_history Family history DM1 family history: yes / no / unknown Demographic
cataracts Cataracts Baseline cataracts yes / no Ophthalmic

3. Which covariates does each method retain?

Dark cell = share of splits in which the method retained the covariate; ● = retained in ≥ 70% of splits. Top block: covariate-modelling methods; bottom block: machine-learning models (tuned). Columns are ordered by overall agreement. Direction is on the improvement scale (from LASSO coefficients). The prior comes from the pre-data mechanistic hypothesis sheet.

Mexiletine

Covariate Retained by (continuous) Retained by (responder) Effect direction (data) Hypothesis-sheet prior Verdict
Myotonia severity 20/20 11/20 higher → more improvement strong, expects higher → more improvement Retained & clinically plausible
Disease duration 8/20 0/20 higher → less improvement none Occasionally retained (<50% of methods)
Family history 4/20 2/20 none Occasionally retained (<50% of methods)
CTG repeat length 1/20 6/20 none Occasionally retained (<50% of methods)
Smoking 0/20 3/20 moderate, expects higher → less improvement Occasionally retained (<50% of methods)

Mexiletine acts on the muscle sodium channel to relieve myotonia: patients with more baseline myotonia have more to gain (and more to regress).

Oligonucleotide

Covariate Retained by (continuous) Retained by (responder) Effect direction (data) Hypothesis-sheet prior Verdict
CTG repeat length 16/20 14/20 higher → more improvement strong Retained & clinically plausible
Disease duration 2/20 5/20 higher → more improvement moderate, expects higher → less improvement Occasionally retained (<50% of methods)
Family history 9/20 0/20 none Occasionally retained (<50% of methods)
Muscle strength 2/20 2/20 higher → less improvement strong Strong prior, not retained by most methods
Somatic mosaicism 1/20 0/20 higher → more improvement strong Strong prior, not retained by most methods

The oligonucleotide targets the toxic CUG-repeat RNA, so repeat burden is the plausible driver; direction was left open by the hypothesis sheet.

Tideglusib

Covariate Retained by (continuous) Retained by (responder) Effect direction (data) Hypothesis-sheet prior Verdict
Cognitive function 20/20 20/20 higher → less improvement strong, expects higher → less improvement Retained & clinically plausible
Disease duration 14/20 0/20 higher → less improvement weak Retained, weak/no prior: needs validation
Muscle strength 5/20 1/20 strong, expects higher → less improvement Strong prior, not retained by most methods
Cataracts 1/20 4/20 none Occasionally retained (<50% of methods)
Myotonia severity 1/20 2/20 higher → more improvement weak Occasionally retained (<50% of methods)

Tideglusib (GSK-3 inhibitor) is aimed at CNS involvement; lower baseline cognition = more room to improve.

How 'retained' is defined for each method

Method What it is Covariate counts as retained when (in a given split)
lm / glm Linear (logistic) regression on all covariates p < 0.05
Stepwise (4 variants) Adds/drops covariates by AIC or BIC kept in final model with p < 0.05
Best subset Exhaustive search, best by BIC (continuous only) kept with p < 0.05
Ridge / LASSO / Elastic net Penalised regression; ridge never drops a covariate, so it is not scored for retention non-zero coefficient
Polynomial / Piecewise / Spline Curved effects on the 4 covariates most correlated with the target (re-chosen inside each fit) drop-one F/χ² test p < 0.05
Smoothing spline One smooth curve on the single strongest covariate correlation p < 0.05
GAM Smooth term for every continuous covariate smooth/linear term p < 0.05
PCR (PCA) Regression on principal components; no covariate-level result n/a
Logistic, tree, forest, SVM, KNN, XGBoost, MLP Machine learning, untuned and tuned (GridSearchCV) permutation importance on test > 0 (95% CI) and ≥ 10% of the model's top importance

4. Take-aways for the slides

  • One covariate per arm is picked by essentially every method; the remaining covariates are inconsistent between methods and between splits and should not be presented as drivers.
  • The retained drivers match the mechanism of each drug (Mexiletine - myotonia; Oligonucleotide - repeat burden; Tideglusib - cognition) where the hypothesis sheet had a prior.
  • Which covariates matter is method-independent; which method predicts best is not: tree ensembles and simple penalised/stepwise models are equivalent in Mexiletine (ensembles are ahead only in Tideglusib, behind in Oligonucleotide), flexible networks/KNN/SVM are worse on ~120 patients, and nothing rescues the weakly predictable Oligonucleotide arm.

5. Caveats

  • Test sets are 41-43 patients; one patient moves a split's metric, hence the multi-seed design. Splits share the same 500 patients, so the 20 results are not independent replicates; SDs understate uncertainty about new patients.
  • 'Retained' uses within-method p-values (after selection for stepwise/best subset, so optimistic) and permutation importance for ML; stability across splits is the multiplicity guard, not a formal correction.
  • Correlated covariates (CTG vs myotonia severity; onset vs duration) share credit, so a retained covariate can be a proxy.

Reproduce: bash split_1to3/seed_sensitivity/run_seeds.sh then python split_1to3/seed_sensitivity/src/clean_report.py. Figures as PNG in split_1to3/reports/figs/. AI use: Claude Code wrote and ran the code and drafted the text; numbers are regenerated by the scripts.
